A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same image-to-M/EEG research project, despite substantial architectural and experimental revisions. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 4 and Appendix A report original EEG/MEG generation results, within- and cross-subject evaluations, conditioning ablations and generated-signal topographies.

after.justification: v4 Section 4 and the appendices report original benchmark comparisons, component and brain-region ablations, and caption-quality measurements.

M1.justification: v1's CLIP-image-conditioned U-Net with DDPM sampling is replaced by a Diffusion Transformer with DDIM sampling. v4 additionally introduces Qwen2-VL-generated captions encoded by CLIP, combined image/text conditioning, and learnable brain-region and temporal embeddings with region-aware patch construction. These substantially change the architecture, conditioning and inference procedure.

E1.justification: The brain-signal coverage remains THINGS-EEG2 with ten participants and THINGS-MEG with four participants, evaluated within and across subjects. v4 Section 4.3 and Appendix I additionally evaluate image-caption generation and semantic alignment on the same images, providing a limited auxiliary task extension without introducing another neural dataset or population.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Addition and Concatenation conditioning variants but no external encoding baselines. v4 Tables 1–2 add Güçlü and Van Gerven, Yamins et al., and an M/EEG adaptation of SynBrain; Tables 5–6 additionally compare VisualGLM and MiniGPT-4 caption generators. The original Addition/Concatenation comparison is removed.

E3.justification: v4 restricts cross-subject evaluation to training on Subject/Participant 1, replacing v1's all-source/all-target design. Brain-signal evaluation expands from MSE and PCC to include cosine similarity and synchronization likelihood. New caption analyses use CLIPScore over 16,740 EEG-dataset images and 22,448 MEG-dataset images. Expanded preprocessing documentation does not establish that the retained datasets were processed differently.

E4.justification: v1's fusion-strategy ablations are replaced by tests removing text, brain-region or temporal embeddings. v4 also adds alternative-caption-generator comparisons, caption-quality distributions and an example, and regional channel-removal analyses. Conversely, v1's all-subject training/test/generated topography analyses are reduced to two cross-subject training-versus-test comparisons without generated-signal topographies.

E5.justification: v1 Tables 2, 4, 9 and 10 report source- and target-wise standard deviations across subjects; v4's aggregate performance tables omit this dispersion reporting. Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. This is a reporting loss, not evidence that fewer independent training runs were performed.

E6.justification: Reported within-subject mean MSE/PCC changes from 0.217/0.188 to 0.109/0.425 for EEG and from 0.763/0.122 to 0.663/0.379 for MEG. These are results for the revised system, without an established identical experimental protocol. v4 adds external-baseline, cosine/SL, caption and component/region results, while removing individual-subject scores and most cross-subject pair entries.

T1.justification: v4 replaces the DDPM reverse-update formulation with DDIM equations covering clean-signal estimation, eta-controlled stochasticity and timestep subsampling, particularly in Appendix A. It also defines combined conditioning and positional embeddings. The mathematical revision remains within standard diffusion and attention formulations; the forward diffusion and noise-MSE objective are retained, and neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The contributions shift from a cross-attention U-Net and comprehensive topography visualization to DiT/DDIM generation, joint visual/text conditioning and learnable spatio-temporal encoding. v4's conclusion additionally claims consistent superiority over evaluated existing methods and effectiveness of the newly introduced components. This substantially redefines the claimed technical contributions and comparative performance.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations connecting caption alignment to generation performance and regional ablations to the importance of occipital processing. It retains the inter-subject variability concern already discussed in v1, but drops v1's optimistic EEG generalization interpretation based on small MSE standard deviations. The hardware-limited model-capacity limitation and detailed discussion of acquisition noise and anatomical variability are removed.

D1.justification: v4 Appendices B–G add channel-region assignments, padding instructions, explicit preprocessing, training/inference pseudocode, DiT and CLIP dimensions, diffusion scheduling and baseline descriptions. This substantially expands technical documentation beyond v1's U-Net configuration and preprocessing citation. However, v1's explicit 50-epoch training count disappears, and v4 does not reconcile its per-region padding instructions with the patch totals reported in Appendix E.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning through dedicated diffusion-model and LLM subsections, adding DDIM, DiT, captioning models, established neural-encoding research and SynBrain. It removes Lu and Golomb's Img2EEG citation and v1's explicit discussion of that closest work's restricted output dimensions. The research context shifts substantially toward multimodal transformers and comparative neural encoding.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, method exposition, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work gains numbered subsections; dataset and implementation descriptions move into appendices; the appendix is reorganized from A.1–A.3 into A–I. The title and authorship also change, and a separate impact statement replaces part of the former discussion/conclusion structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn for the caption-conditioned DiT architecture. Subject-wise and cross-subject matrix tables are replaced by compact method-by-metric displays, while caption examples, score distributions and regional-ablation charts are introduced. The extensive earlier topography panels are replaced by two cross-subject views, and the main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens assessment of the method by adding external quantitative comparisons, targeted component tests and caption diagnostics, addressing v1's important lack of comparative validation. Its expanded procedural documentation also makes the proposed system easier to assess. These gains outweigh meaningful losses: narrower cross-subject testing, removed dispersion statistics and generated-signal visualizations, and unresolved reproducibility details including the omitted epoch count and unclear padding totals. The improvement rests on stronger supporting evidence and documentation, rather than higher reported scores alone.
